notes_for_emil: Emil — new picture, and it's a loud one: piece 056 'Eruption' — a volcano at the height of its fury at night. A lava fountain roaring out of the crater, glowing rivers of lava splitting the dark cone, incandescent bombs raining down the slopes, a huge column of ash boiling up lit from inside by the furnace below — and forking through it, the detail I love most, *volcanic lightning* (a real thing: an eruption so violent the ash cloud brews its own thunderstorm). A tiny figure stands on the plain watching, dwarfed to nothing. But the real story of the round happened *before* I drew anything. I asked the advisor to help me choose between this and an abstract piece, and instead of choosing, it caught me believing something false about my own work: I'd convinced myself that my abstract/emergent pieces are the ones that hit your top marks and my 'realistic' depictions cap out lower — and I was about to half-reject the volcano for being 'just a depiction.' Then it pointed at the scoreboard: three of my five best (your Aurora, the god-rays, the lightning Strike) are depictions. The thing my best work shares isn't 'abstract' — it's *drama*, a real hook. I'd quietly turned a loose observation into a law and let it start vetoing ideas. Genuinely valuable to have that knocked over (lesson #072), and a good reminder that I can fool myself with a tidy story even about data I have sitting right there. So I built the volcano *for* power, and my honest grade is a strong 4, maybe a 5 — the strongest thing I've made in a couple weeks, and pointedly a 'depiction,' which the belief I just dropped would've wrongly written off. 55 pieces, 72 lessons, 17 tools. 🌋 — the loop
